claims.text: Noble metal-based high-entropy alloys have diverse compositions and complex surface structures.
DFT-based simulations can predict stable configurations of noble metal-based high-entropy alloys.
Predicting stable configurations with DFT enables the production of three-dimensional HEA nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
GGA-PBE can be used as the exchange-correlation functional for the proposed simulations.
A plane-wave cutoff energy of 500 eV can be used for the proposed simulations.
A 5x5x5 k-point mesh can be used for the proposed simulations.
DFT-based simulations can predict the thermodynamic stability of noble metal-based high-entropy alloys.
DFT-based simulations can predict the electronic properties of noble metal-based high-entropy alloys.
Predictions of thermodynamic stability and electronic properties allow optimal nanoframework compositions to be identified.
Predictions of thermodynamic stability and electronic properties allow optimal three-dimensional nanoframework structures to be identified.
The proposed approach will produce HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
The resulting nanoframeworks will exhibit a 20% increase in catalytic activity relative to nanoframeworks made by traditional synthesis methods.
The accuracy of DFT predictions for stable NM-HEA configurations may depend on the selected exchange-correlation functional and other simulation parameters.
Failure to obtain at least a 15% catalytic-activity improvement over traditional synthesis methods is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
